claims.citation: New York Herald, 17 June 1866, p. 2, col. 5
New York Herald, 17 June 1866, p. 1, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
The steamship Queen left Liverpool simultaneously
with the City of Paris for New York.

Steamship "The Queen" (Br.), Trogan, Liverpool via Queenstown
June 6, with mdse. and 380 pass. to National Steam Navigation Co.
June 7, saw an Inman steamer, bound E; 11th inst., in lat. 48 38, long.
27 45, passed a Bremen steamship, bound E; 10th ins., in lat. 49 50,
long. 22 19, passed a bark-rigged steamer, bound E.

claims.citation: Lloyd's List, 3 July 1866, p. 6, col. 3 (British Newspaper Archive)
New York Herald, 20 June 1866, p. 5, col. 6
claims.verbatim:
Steamship The Queen (Br), Grogan, Liverpool, via Queens-
town June 6, with mdse and 380[?] passengers, to the National
Steam Navigation Co. June 10, lat 49 50, lon 22 19, passed
a bark rigged steamer bound E; same day, saw an Inman
steamer, also bound E; 11th, lat 48 38, lon 27 45, passed a Bre-
men steamer, bound E.
